summary: Douglas County, OR: first tower 1949, storm-damaged 1962, replacement cab 1963, removed 2017; sources disagree on who took it down.

facts.design: First tower of 40 or 44 feet with an L-4 cab (sources differ); 1963 replacement with a 14 by 14 foot flat-top ODF cab on a timber tower of 50 to 55 feet
facts.status_note: Removed in 2017. Sources differ on who took it down (the Oregon Department of Forestry or the Weyerhaeuser Company) and on whether it was removed or destroyed.

staffing.status: staffed in summer until the late 2000s

facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry, with the Douglas Forest Protective Association as cooperator

events.note: First tower on the site; the register and firelookout.com say 40 feet, the Former Fire Lookout Sites entry says 44 feet
A February 1950 News-Review item, quoted by Kemnow, still called for completion before fire season
Minta King employed as summer lookout, per a June 1955 News-Review item quoted by Kemnow
Lost in the Columbus Day storm per the register, the Former Fire Lookout Sites entry and firelookout.com; Kemnow says it was severely damaged
14 by 14 foot ODF flat-top cab on a timber tower; the Former Fire Lookout Sites entry gives a 55-foot tower with an Amort cab
FFLA report says the Oregon Department of Forestry removed it; Kemnow says Weyerhaeuser removed it citing safety; the Former Fire Lookout Sites entry says destroyed
Registered November 14, 2019 in the Former Fire Lookout Sites register

corrections.why: The record uses the register's replacement date. The Former Fire Lookout Sites entry and firelookout.com both date the first lookout on the site to 1949; 1963 is the replacement tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1949 tower is the first on the site, and the register's 1963 date is for the replacement tower and cab. Kemnow's site, quoting a February 1950 News-Review item, suggests the lookout was still being finished in 1950.

All sources agree the lookout is gone. They disagree on the 2017 event: the FFLA report says the Oregon Department of Forestry removed it, Kemnow says Weyerhaeuser did, and the Former Fire Lookout Sites entry says it was destroyed.

notes_for_editor: Record elevation 987.2 m matches the register's 3,239 ft; the Former Fire Lookout Sites entry and firelookout.com give 3,346 ft (about 1,020 m). Left unchanged here. No source read establishes access today. A web search found no decisive account of who removed the tower; Oregon Department of Forestry or Weyerhaeuser records may settle it. The record's built correction (1963 to 1949) is a proposal for human review.
